shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures rose on Monday after a six-session losing streak, as a rally in oil prices and concerns that heavy rain in top producer Thailand will disrupt tapping supported the market.($1 = 156.0000 yen)($1 = 6.7108 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures rose on Monday after a six-session losing streak, as a rally in oil prices and concerns that heavy rain in top producer Thailand will disrupt tapping supported the market.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was up 9 yen, or 2.1%, at 437 yen ($2.80) per kg, as of 0205 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 425 yuan, or 2.26%, to 19,195 yuan ($2,860.31) per metric ton.
The most-active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) surged 925 yuan, or 6.2%, to 15,845 yuan per ton.

Oil prices extended gains as tit-for-tat strikes between the U.S. and Iran on vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz and other areas heightened concerns of a prolonged supply disruption from the Middle East.
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.

The narrowing price gap between synthetic and natural rubber has prompted some downstream companies to raise the share of natural rubber in their formulations, creating additional marginal demand, analysts from broker Guoyuan Futures said in a note.
Top rubber producer Thailand's meteorological agency warned of severe rains and flash floods from September 6 to 12.
Persistent rainfall continues to disrupt tapping in Thailand's main producing areas, tightening raw material supply, the analysts said.
El Niño, which is expected to peak from September to November, raises the risk of further production cuts, they said.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 240.3 U.S. cents per kg, up 3%.
